verdicts.quote: The user finds an entry point in the designated org that opens the bot.
verdicts.missing: Which Salesforce surface hosts the bot (record page, utility bar, Experience Cloud, Flow) and what context it receives.

verdicts.quote: With an existing record open in Salesforce, submitting text that omits the record's data sends none of that record's fields or attachments to Grok.
The bot does not automatically include Salesforce record data in Grok input.
A signed-in user without bot authorization cannot invoke Grok through the bot, including through a directly opened bot entry point.
verdicts.missing: The concrete permission mechanism for use, and what authority is required to administer (C-35 says only 'applicable setup authority').

verdicts.quote: When two users submit concurrently, each sees only their own result, including if the results arrive in reverse order.
Inspecting the bot page, its browser requests, and its user-visible errors does not expose the configured credential.
verdicts.missing: Where the credential is stored (Named/External Credential or protected setting) and that it never appears in code, metadata or logs.

verdicts.quote: While an accepted submission is awaiting its result, the user can tell that processing is in progress.
verdicts.missing: The mechanism by which the interface learns the answer arrived (platform event, polling, LMS, etc.).

verdicts.quote: Activating submit twice for the same pending send produces one Grok submission for that send.
verdicts.missing: Idempotency for a retried or re-enqueued async job so the same reply is not posted twice.

verdicts.quote: When xAI responds with a server error in the 500–599 range, the user sees a service failure for the submission.
An xAI rate-limit response with status 429 results in a user-visible rate-limit outcome.
verdicts.missing: Backoff and retry policy for rate limiting or quota exhaustion.

verdicts.quote: If the bot displays text from an incomplete response, the user can tell the displayed reply is incomplete.
After a user closes the bot and opens it again, the earlier interaction is not available as a saved transcript in Salesforce.
verdicts.missing: Any stored record shape (role, status, timestamps, model identifier, token/usage counts); spec chooses no persistence but states no record of requests or usage.

verdicts.quote: The bot does not create saved Salesforce conversation history.
submitting text that omits the record's data sends none of that record's fields or attachments to Grok.
verdicts.missing: How personal data that users type into prompts is handled.

verdicts.quote: When Grok rejects the request for excessive input length, the user sees that the prompt needs to be shortened.
verdicts.missing: Whether prior turns are sent as context, and what is trimmed or summarised at what size.

verdicts.quote: A valid prompt measured at the exact published maximum proceeds past the bot's length validation.
The operator can determine the exact model identifier in use for the development org.
verdicts.missing: A switch to turn the bot off, a way to change the model, and a view of failed requests.

verdicts.quote: A deployment attempt aimed at a production business org makes no changes there.
verdicts.missing: Per-environment configuration and credential differences, deployment method, and code-coverage requirement.

verdicts.quote: The deployed bot or its operating instructions give the exact positive deadline in seconds, measured from acceptance of the submission.
verdicts.missing: The actual latency target or deadline value.

verdicts.quote: While an accepted submission is awaiting its result, the user can tell that processing is in progress.
verdicts.missing: An initial empty state and a deliberately designed interface for the loading, error and refused states.

verdicts.quote: An existing workflow or automation outside the bot still produces its prior observable result for the same triggering inputs after the bot is installed or used.
